Brown sought to warn her 1999 interlocutors against the dangers of political melancholy at a moment when the global Left was suffering another round of historic losses. She was especially concerned about the tendency among traditional Leftists to scapegoat identity politics for these losses, even as they remained anachronistically attached to a reductive materialism and belief in historical teleology.
